clue.text: Rarely digress from prima donna scandal?

definitions.note: a verb meaning to wander off the point, flagged as a rarely used word

parts.note: a prima donna is an operatic diva
-gate is the suffix tagged onto scandals since Watergate

explanation.surface: Someone seldom strays from talking about the latest scandal involving an opera star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' belongs with the definition: the word is marked rare or literary in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary, seldom-used verb for wandering off the subject, so a rare synonym of digress.

clue.text: Making new version of Annie's hard, even a one-off musical

indicators.note: remaking a version of something rearranges what is given, so these letters are shuffled
one being off means the letter for one is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: the name and its possessive s, taken letter by letter
one is I, the Roman numeral
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revival of the musical Annie is hard to make, even for a one-off show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-off' tells you to drop I (one) from ANNIES; the remaining letters with HARD, EVEN and A are rearranged under 'Making new version of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Broadway stage show about a lonely teenager, which won the Tony for best musical.

clue.text: Musical that might be very good or very bad

definitions.meaning: the stage show about the witches of Oz
the word means evil, and in slang also excellent

explanation.surface: A musical that reviewers might find either brilliant or dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oz-witches stage show, and an adjective meaning evil that slang turns into excellent.

clue.text: Bit of choral singing Hot Press briefly hammered

indicators.note: hammered means beaten out of shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A short piece of choir music was savaged by the Hot Press, an Irish music magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims PRESS to PRES; HOT plus PRES is then rearranged under 'hammered'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek drama, a section of an ode sung by the chorus while moving one way, so a stanza of choral song.

clue.text: Satirise musical overdoing carnal knowledge, for starters

indicators.note: for starters means just the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A critic sends up a musical that goes too far with its sex scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to ridicule or parody them, a plain verb synonym of lampooning.

clue.text: Worried less about one newspaper initially concealing Conservative plots

indicators.note: concealing means the scrambled letters hide the next piece inside them
worried in the sense of shaken about, so the letters are rearranged
about in the sense of moved around, so the letters of less are already being stirred before the rest join them

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word newspaper

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A worried paper prints less about one politician while a Tory covers up plots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' and 'about' together scramble less, I and N into S...LINES, and 'concealing' hides the Tory after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots of novels or films are their narratives, a straightforward synonym in the plural.

clue.text: Italian singer finally in charge in English opera company

indicators.note: in means the last pieces sit inside the opera company's initials

parts.note: ENO is English National Opera, based at the London Coliseum

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word singer

explanation.surface: An Italian tenor ends up leading an English opera company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian singer' looks like the definition, pointing at Caruso, but 'singer finally' gives only R; the definition is just 'Italian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Italian male first name, the counterpart of Henry, borne by the tenor Caruso.

clue.text: Good sense to include winter pear in what restaurant may offer

indicators.note: to include means the sense word wraps round the pear

parts.note: wit is good sense or intelligence
Winter Nelis is a variety of pear that ripens in winter

explanation.surface: A restaurant shows good sense putting a seasonal pear on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: NELIS is the Winter Nelis, a late-ripening dessert pear.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant offers diners a card of bottles and glasses to choose from, which is this phrase.

clue.text: See 19
Musical scores for No 1s?

definitions.note: a number one is the closest setting on hair clippers, hence a very short trim; the question mark marks the cryptic example

parts.note: the 1960s hippie stage show
to score is to cut a line into something, so scores are slashes

explanation.surface: A musical scores for its headline acts, the number ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1s' looks like chart toppers but means the shortest clipper setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A number one is the shortest buzz trim at a barber's, so these are examples of short trims.

clue.text: South African club has male member that is touring Irish county shortly

parts.note: knob is slang for the penis

indicators.note: shortly means the county's name is cut by its last letter

parts.note: Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A South African club with a male member is on tour round an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims KERRY to KERR. 'touring' is loose: the pieces simply run on in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stick with a heavy round head used as a weapon by Zulu and other southern African peoples.

clue.text: Butt of a gendarme's covered

indicators.note: covered means the letters lie concealed within these words

explanation.surface: A gendarme's backside is covered.
explanation.definitionFit: The butt of a cigarette is the stub left after smoking, slang synonym.

clue.text: See 2
Musical seen by one lecturer during a month off

indicators.note: during means the next pieces fall inside the scrambled month
off in the sense of not right, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A lecturer goes to see a musical while taking a month off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles A MONTH into HAM...TON, and 'during' puts I and L in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop stage show about the American founding father is a famous example.

clue.text: See 17
Number clever enough for game show

parts.note: ten is a number
able means competent or clever enough to do something

explanation.surface: A contestant is bright enough to go on a TV quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: A British ITV quiz hosted by Warwick Davis in which contestants name top-ten lists.

clue.text: There's not so much about military intelligence in a musical, commonly

indicators.note: about means the word for not so much goes round the intelligence letters

parts.note: less means not so much
MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5

explanation.surface: A musical apparently contains less about military intelligence than you might expect.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday shortened title of the Boublil and Schonberg show based on Victor Hugo's novel.

clue.text: Into pieces like a French and German article

parts.note: as means like
un is French for a
der is the German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: Something falls apart in the manner of a French and a German article.
explanation.definitionFit: To be torn into parts, as in the wedding vow let no man put apart, is the plain sense.

clue.text: Panel show score indicating pretty good musical

parts.note: a mark of eight on a scale ... is a fairly high score
the Lloyd Webber show based on T S Eliot's poems

explanation.surface: A panel show gives a mark suggesting a musical was decent.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a British Channel 4 comedy panel show built round opinion poll results.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British comedy quiz on Channel 4 where teams guess survey statistics.

clue.text: Phone in, say, about making 5 orange or lilac

indicators.note: in means the phone word goes inside the jumbled say
about in the sense of turned around, so the letters of say are rearranged

parts.note: to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Call in and say something about making orange or lilac.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' is the answer to 5 down, MOCK, so the definition reads mock orange or lilac.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries give this as the name of both the philadelphus shrub and the lilac genus.

clue.text: Frightfully honest — extremely lazy in secret

indicators.note: frightfully suggests being in a fright, so the letters are thrown about
extremely means the two outside letters of lazy

explanation.surface: Someone is terribly truthful, and also secretly very idle.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for doing something covertly, without others noticing.

clue.text: Somewhat excessive number

parts.note: part of the word excessive is XC, the Roman numeral for the number

explanation.surface: A number that is a bit over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' points to a part of 'excessive': its second and third letters, XC, are Roman for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a number, here written as the Roman XC.

clue.text: Number of pills required by queasy sea dog

indicators.note: queasy means feeling sick, so the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: A seasick old sailor needs some tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount of medicine prescribed at one time, so how many tablets to take.

clue.text: Sleep? Perchance, except those seen in schools in dorm, oddly

indicators.note: in means the trimmed word sits inside the odd letters of dorm
oddly means the first and third letters of dorm
except means those letters are taken away from the start of perchance

parts.note: perch are fish, which swim in schools

explanation.surface: Hamlet's 'To sleep, perchance to dream' gets mangled in a school dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Sleep is a celebrated British ballet star, so 'Sleep?' is a definition by example; the fish in 'those seen in schools' swim in shoals, not classrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayne Sleep, the small British ballet star of the Royal Ballet, is an example.

clue.text: Flooding, with one sister (not Ida) affected

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: affected in the sense of disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flood strikes, and every sister except Ida is affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not Ida' looks like an instruction to delete IDA, but the words NOT IDA are themselves the letters rearranged, into DATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge of water spreading over land, a straightforward noun synonym.

clue.text: Singer featuring in musical today

indicators.note: featuring in means the letters appear within these two words

explanation.surface: A singer stars in a musical today.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice part between soprano and tenor, and the person who sings it.

clue.text: See 10
See 19
Time musical is current

parts.note: Jonathan Larson's rock show set in New York's East Village

explanation.surface: It's time a musical was up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an adjective meaning present, but it is a flowing current: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flowing stream of water, and this is a big English one.

clue.text: Former non-flyer reporting dull conversation

indicators.note: reporting means the words are as heard, spoken

parts.note: grey means dull, and talk is conversation

explanation.surface: An ex-pilot's account amounts to boring chitchat.
explanation.walkthrough: The match is loose: the setter later admitted that GREY TALK does not quite say the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flightless seabird of the North Atlantic, hunted to extinction in the 1840s.
